name: Lithium

tolerance.full: No significant tolerance develops to therapeutic effects

toxicities: Lithium has a narrow therapeutic window (0.6-1.2 mM blood concentration). Toxicity occurs above 1.5 mM. Symptoms: nausea, vomiting, tremor, confusion, seizures, coma, death. Chronic toxicity: kidney damage, thyroid dysfunction.
summary: Lithium is a naturally occurring alkali metal used primarily as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder. It inhibits GSK-3β activating the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, and substitutes for sodium in voltage-gated channels. Recent research suggests endogenous lithium deficiency may be an early molecular event in Alzheimer's disease.
effectsSummary: Mood stabilization, reduced manic episodes, suicide prevention, neuroprotection via GSK-3β inhibition, enhanced neurogenesis, reduced amyloid deposition. Low doses (5-25mg elemental lithium as orotate) may have nootropic and anti-aging effects.
dosageRemark: Lithium carbonate therapeutic dose: 600-1800mg daily (110-330mg elemental lithium), blood level 0.6-1.2mM requires monitoring. Low-dose lithium orotate supplements (5-25mg elemental lithium) available without prescription. Lithium orotate has better brain penetration and avoids Aβ plaque sequestration compared to carbonate.
generalRisks: At therapeutic doses: hypothyroidism, kidney damage, weight gain, tremor, cognitive dulling. At low supplement doses (5-25mg): minimal side effects expected. Must avoid dehydration and monitor kidney function at higher doses.
longtermRisks: Chronic high-dose lithium therapy: hypothyroidism, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, kidney damage, weight gain, tremor. Low-dose supplementation: long-term risks not well characterized but expected to be minimal.
saferUse: Monitor blood lithium levels if using therapeutic doses
Avoid dehydration and NSAIDs if on lithium therapy
Do not combine with diuretics without medical supervision
Low-dose orotate form is safer for non-prescription use (5-25mg elemental lithium/day)
